description: Claims this project makes about itself, and the experiments that decide them. Regenerate statuses with: python -m validation.scientific_method run

claims.statement: The 240 generated vectors form the E8 root system: norm^2 = 2, integral inner products, no duplicates.
claims.evidence: 240 roots, all norm^2=2.0, inner products in [-2.0, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 2.0], 0 duplicates

claims.statement: Each geometric energy term is a non-constant function of the state x.
claims.evidence: worst term OctahedralEnergy: 300/300 distinct values over the sphere
claims.note: Revision 1 of the code failed this: terms read only the neighbour set, never x.

history.statement: Each geometric energy term is a non-constant function of the state x.
history.evidence: All 7 terms returned identical values for x and for an unrelated vector; energy took <=10 distinct values over the whole sphere.
history.superseded_because: Claim retained unchanged; the implementation was corrected instead (gas/energy_terms.py revision 2).

claims.statement: No energy term degenerates to a constant over the sphere.
claims.note: Targets the specific revision-1 collapses: TetrahedralEnergy == 1/3 and GoldenEnergy == |1-phi|.

history.statement: No energy term degenerates to a constant over the sphere.
history.evidence: TetrahedralEnergy was exactly 0.333333 and GoldenEnergy exactly 0.618034 at every sampled point.
history.superseded_because: Implementation corrected: tetrahedral now scores x-to-neighbour cosines, golden now scores shell-distance ratios from x.

claims.statement: Analytic gradients agree with central finite differences to better than 1e-5 relative error.
claims.note: Standard code verification. Revision 1 had no analytic gradient to check.

claims.statement: Every energy term has a nonzero gradient with respect to x.
claims.evidence: smallest gradient norm across all terms and samples: 9.661e-03 (HexagonalEnergy)

history.statement: Every energy term has a nonzero gradient with respect to x.
history.evidence: ||grad|| was exactly 0.000e+00 for all 7 terms: the finite-difference gradient perturbed x while holding the neighbour set fixed, and the terms ignored x.
history.superseded_because: Implementation corrected; gradients are now analytic.

claims.statement: The recorded energy changes over the course of an optimization run.

history.statement: The recorded energy changes over the course of an optimization run.
history.evidence: 1000 iterations produced exactly 1 distinct energy value: the proposal was scored against the current point's neighbour set, so delta_E was identically 0.
history.superseded_because: step() now re-evaluates the proposal under its own neighbourhood.

claims.statement: GAS reduces the geometric energy below its starting value.
The --all-terms flag changes the computation performed.

history.statement: The --all-terms flag changes the computation performed.
history.evidence: Output was identical to 9 decimal places with and without the flag: _compute_weights returned 3 weights regardless of term count, so zip() silently discarded terms 4-7.
history.superseded_because: _compute_weights now returns one weight per term and raises on a count mismatch.

claims.statement: The annealing schedule decays with the iteration index.
claims.note: THEORY.md 9.2 rests on this: its proof sketch asserts sigma_t, T_t -> 0.

history.statement: The annealing schedule decays with the iteration index.
history.evidence: sigma_t and T_t depended only on rho, never on t; sigma_t stayed within [0.0452, 0.0500] for the entire run.
history.superseded_because: A cooling factor exp(-t/tau_anneal) was added to eta_t, alpha_t, sigma_t and T_t.

claims.statement: Runs are reproducible from a seed, independent of the global NumPy RNG state.
claims.evidence: two runs under different global seeds: 0.275303544465 vs 0.275303544465

history.statement: Runs are reproducible from a seed.
history.evidence: The solver drew from the global np.random state, so any other code touching that state changed the result.
history.superseded_because: The solver now takes an injectable numpy Generator.

claims.statement: Despite non-convexity, annealing on E8 converges reliably -- GAS finds lower energy than uniform random sampling at equal evaluation budget.
claims.evidence: GAS mean 0.280879 vs random 0.284600 (+1.3%), GAS wins 5/8 seeds
claims.note: The headline performance claim. Requires GAS to win at least 6 of 8 seeds against the baseline.

claims.statement: Under the GAS update rule the expected energy decreases: E[E_{t+1}] <= E_t + O(sigma_t^2).
claims.evidence: mean one-step dE = -0.003779 over 120 states, bound sigma^2 = 0.002500; 77% of steps were non-increasing
claims.note: Revision-1 premise (deterministic gradient descent) was false because gradients were identically zero; with revision-2 energy terms the premise holds, so the lemma is now empirically decidable. Registered experiment expected_energy_decreases.

history.statement: Under the GAS update rule the expected energy decreases: E[E_{t+1}] <= E_t + O(sigma_t^2).
history.superseded_because: Revision-1 premise (deterministic gradient descent) was false because gradients were identically zero; with revision-2 energy terms the premise holds, so the lemma is now empirically decidable. Registered experiment expected_energy_decreases.

claims.statement: With probability 1, GAS converges to a local minimum of E(x) on the E8 manifold.
claims.note: Labelled a Theorem but supported only by a four-bullet sketch appealing to 'standard simulated annealing theory'. Those results require a cooling schedule of order 1/log(t); the implemented schedule is geometric, which does not satisfy their hypotheses. No proof is given here.

claims.statement: For problems whose global optimum has rho_coset > rho_min, GAS finds the global minimum with high probability.
claims.note: Explicitly labelled a conjecture, which is honest. Deciding it needs a problem family with known global optima; none exists in this repository yet.

claims.statement: Empirical validation on known problems shows global recovery.
claims.evidence: No validation study, dataset, benchmark or result table exists anywhere in the repository. The sentence cites work that was never done.
claims.note: Removed from THEORY.md. Recorded here so the removal is auditable rather than silent.

claims.statement: Sphere packing, supply chain and energy system examples validate the framework against known optimal solutions.
claims.evidence: No examples/ directory, no benchmark comparing against known optima. benchmarks/random_baseline.py compares GAS against random search only.
claims.note: Rewritten in README.md as planned work rather than completed validation.

claims.statement: Conventional equation architecture operates at 0.5 sigma quality, with a 94% defect rate across economics, AI training and corporate metrics.
claims.evidence: No dataset, sample frame, population definition, coding protocol or inter-rater procedure is given for any of the percentages. The sigma levels are computed from figures that were not measured.
claims.note: Moved to legacy/. To make this testable, define the population of 'equations' being sampled, the operational definition of a 'defect', and the coding procedure -- then revise this claim and register an experiment.

claims.statement: Robots are 30x-100x more energy expensive than efficient human workers on a full lifecycle basis.
claims.evidence: No citations, no lifecycle inventory, no system boundary and no source for any of the kWh/day figures. The ranges are asserted, not derived.
claims.note: Moved to legacy/. To make this testable, cite a published lifecycle assessment, state the system boundary, and register an experiment recomputing the ratio from the cited inventory.

claims.statement: The meta-layer's geometric regularization term influences the decoded N-dimensional solution.
claims.evidence: min ||grad R_geo|| = 3.032e-01; turning lambda_3 off moves the decoded solution by at least 7.166e-01
claims.note: With revision-1 energy terms the R_geo gradient measured ~3e-11, so lambda_3 was inert and the 'geometric coherence' regularizer did nothing.
